1. (Currently amended) A method of treating a brain, comprising: inserting an elongated device into the brain to create a path __between non-adjacent tissue layers__; radially expanding the device to create a working channel along the path __while maintaining separation of the tissue layers__.

2. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein the medical element is an instrument __introduced through the working channel to perform a medical procedure__.

3. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein the medical element is a medicament __delivered through the working channel__.

4. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, further comprising creating an opening in a cranium, and inserting the elongated device through the opening __such that the device is positioned between non-adjacent tissue layers within the brain__.

5. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, further comprising inserting the elongated device between tissue layers within the brain __and maintaining radial expansion of the device to preserve the working channel__.

6. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, further comprising radially contracting and removing the device from the brain __while the working channel remains patent__.

7. (Currently amended) A method of treating a tissue, comprising: placing an elongated device into the tissue to create a path; radially expanding the device against the tissue to radially displace the tissue along the path; radially reinforcing the device against the tissue __by maintaining radial expansion pressure__; and introducing a medical element through the device to perform a medical procedure on the tissue __while the device maintains its radial expansion__.

8. (Currently amended) The method of claim 7, wherein the medical element is an instrument __introduced and manipulated through the working channel__.

9. (Currently amended) The method of claim 7, wherein the medical element is a medicament __infused or injected through the working channel__.

10. (Currently amended) The method of claim 7, further comprising inserting the elongated device between tissue layers __and maintaining the device in an expanded state during introduction of the medical element__.

11. (Currently amended) The method of claim 7, further comprising radially contracting and removing the device from the tissue __after the medical procedure is completed__.

12. (Currently amended) The method of claim 7, further comprising treating the tissue in contact with the device with a haemostatic compound to reduce bleeding __during the procedure__.

13. (Currently amended) A method of treating a tissue, comprising: placing an elongated device, having a first radially expandable body, surrounded by a stent, which is surrounded by a second radially expandable body, into the tissue to create a path; radially expanding the second expandable body against the tissue to radially displace the tissue along the path; radially expanding the first expandable body to radially expand the stent to reinforce the second expandable body against the tissue; radially contracting and removing the first expandable body to create a working channel through the stent __while maintaining the stent in an expanded state__; introducing a medical element through the channel to perform a medical procedure on the tissue __while the stent maintains radial support__; and radially contracting the second expandable body and removing the device from the tissue __after completion of the medical procedure__.

14. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the medical element is an instrument __manipulated through the working channel defined by the stent__.

15. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the medical element is a medicament __delivered through the working channel defined by the stent__.

16. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, further comprising inserting the elongated device between tissue layers __such that the stent provides structural support between the tissue layers__.

17. (Original) The method of claim 13, further comprising treating the tissue in contact with the device with a haemostatic compound to reduce bleeding.
